custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create two active parts for this test, part A and part B.
  • Give parts A and B part numbers that start with the same text, so one search lists both.
  • Make sure no Cycle count is running on the Inventory list.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C847729-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C847729-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • Theme: click your avatar (the AS circle) at the top right; Light and Dark are at the bottom of its menu.
  • A cycle count is running when the Inventory list shows a Count column with Save and Cancel above it; click Cancel to stop it.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Parts A and B are listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 3:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 5:

  • The confirmation stays open: Esc does not close it.

Step 6:

  • The confirmation still stays open: clicking outside it does not close it.

Step 7:

  • The confirmation closes; Edit Inventory Part shows again with Inactive still picked and the green "Active" pill: nothing was saved.

Step 8:

  • The window closes and part A is still listed on the Active tab.

Step 9:

  • The menu opens.

Step 10:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 11:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 12:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation opens, reading "1 part selected."

Step 13:

  • The confirmation stays open: Esc does not close it.

Step 14:

  • The confirmation still stays open: clicking outside it does not close it.

Step 15:

  • The confirmation closes; part B is still ticked and still listed on the Active tab.

Step 16:

  • Bulk mode ends and part B is still listed on the Active tab.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S10-R11a: “The close X at the top right of the confirmation does the same as Cancel: nothing changes, and from the part dialog the user returns to the dialog with the picked status kept. Pressing Esc or clicking outside the confirmation does not close it.”
  • S13-R23: “Cancelling the confirmation saves nothing and returns to the dialog with the picked status kept.”
  • S10-N1: “If the user cancels the confirmation, no part changes status.”
  • S10-R4: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation opens with "{n} parts selected.", or "1 part selected." for one. Raised from the part dialog, it opens with the part number followed by the description, as they stand in the form, with spaces before and after removed.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 19: “(a) Yes, the X stays. It's part of the standard dialog. (b) Yes, it does exactly what Cancel does: nothing changes, and from the part window you return with your picked status kept. Esc and clicking outside don't close it (S10-R11a).”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: boards "3.3 Save asks first", "4.4 Confirm". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • retire-03-p3-3-confirm.png
  • bulk-04-p4-4-confirm.png

The design's own words:

  • “Save raises "Deactivate part?" (S10-R1, S10-R3). It opens with the part number and description (S10-R4), then the three lines of S10-R6, then the optional note (S10-R10). The note here reads "Superseded by N6801-06-04X". The red Deactivate button has Cancel to its left (S10-R11). The bulk confirmation (board 4.4) is the same dialog, built from the design system Modal and Button.”
